re_line: Kim inspects nuclear sites, urges tactical nuke expansion · BOK hikes to 3.25% · Section 301 targets Korea at 15% cap · Russia KADIZ talks · Swiss mission closed
morning_memo: Kim Jong Un inspected nuclear warhead and enrichment facilities, ordering wider tactical nuclear deployment across multiple domains.
Bank of Korea raised its benchmark rate to 3.25%, the third quarter-point hike this year, citing AI-driven growth and inflation.
Trump's new Section 301 tariff proposal targets 14 economies including South Korea, but preserves the existing 15% tariff ceiling from last year's deal.

key_stat.label: Bank of Korea benchmark rate after third hike this year
key_stat.context: The BOK raised its rate to 3.25% on November 26, the third quarter-point increase in 2026, with the governor citing AI-sector growth and inflation as drivers.

imagery_report.label: Destroyer tracking: Kang Kon and Choe Hyon locations confirmed
imagery_report.headline: Daily NK satellite imagery places DPRK destroyers at Mayang Island and Nampo; shipyard expansion visible at Chongjin and Nampo
imagery_report.body: Daily NK satellite imagery analyzed November 24 places the Kang Kon destroyer at Mayang Island naval base and the Choe Hyon at Nampo. Shipyard expansion consistent with additional large-warship construction is visible at both Chongjin and Nampo.

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after more than two years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet. NK News identified a second major east-coast naval base project on Nov 13, beyond the Munchon-area site Kim inspected on Nov 12. Daily NK satellite imagery analyzed Nov 24 places the Kang Kon at Mayang Island naval base and the Choe Hyon at Nampo, with shipyard expansion visible at Chongjin and Nampo consistent with additional large-warship construction.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a 14-daily-round-trip Vladivostok-Rason bus route over the new vehicle bridge, with experts noting the service will likely transport DPRK workers more than Russian tourists.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: NK News Planet Labs satellite imagery analyzed through November 15, 2026 confirms trucks filling Sinuiju customs facility from October 16, the day after the New Yalu River Bridge officially opened, with activity peaking October 19–20. A wall of 40-foot containers bearing Maersk and COSCO markings was visible on the Chinese side. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reported November 18 that Sinuiju markets are overflowing with Chinese goods but a severe cash shortage means almost nobody is buying, with vendors describing a 'trading cliff.' Daily NK reported November 23 that low-income families in Sinuiju are sinking into crisis as market prices for food and daily necessities soar despite state promotion of Sinuiju development as a model for regional growth. NK News reported November 26 that Dandong has announced plans to simplify customs procedures for small-scale border trade and make greater use of the New Yalu River Bridge over the next five years, with border residents within 20 kilometers eligible to register for passes allowing duty-free imports of up to 8,000 yuan per day.

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: Herald Economy reported November 23 that a North Korean vessel marked 'Marine Police' was spotted near Yeonpyeong Island, with the ROK Joint Chiefs confirming they are tracking and monitoring the vessel. As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20, 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is from January 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14, 2026 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a Vladivostok-Rason bus route operating 14 daily round trips. NK News reported November 24 that the Ukrainian military struck the cargo freighter Angara, one of the four vessels in the documented arms-transfer fleet, in a drone attack that also sank the Russian corvette Merkury.

top_stories.headline: Kim inspects nuclear warheads and enrichment sites, rejects recognition from any country
top_stories.body: **Kim Jong Un** inspected three nuclear sites on November 25, a weapons-grade nuclear materials production base, a nuclear-powered equipment production base, and the Nuclear Weapons Institute, where KCNA published photos of him examining warheads, possible naval nuclear reactors, and rows of centrifuge cascades at two uranium enrichment facilities. He ordered wider deployment of tactical nuclear weapons across multiple operational domains and declared North Korea's nuclear status "irreversible," explicitly rejecting the notion of seeking "recognition" from any country. The inspection followed Trump's offer of a bilateral meeting at APEC in Shenzhen, which Kim ignored, and came on the same day NK News reported a ballistic missile engine test occurred during Trump's outreach.

top_stories.headline: Bank of Korea raises rate to 3.25%, third hike this year, as AI boom fuels growth and inflation
top_stories.body: The **Bank of Korea** raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to *3.25%* on November 26, the third such increase in 2026, with the BOK governor citing AI-sector expansion and inflationary pressure as drivers. The central bank also upgraded its 2027 growth outlook. The rate now stands at its highest level in the current cycle.

top_stories.headline: Trump's new Section 301 tariff proposal targets 14 economies but preserves Korea's 15% ceiling
top_stories.body: The Trump administration proposed new tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 against *14 trading partners* over industrial overcapacity, including South Korea, while a senior US official confirmed the proposed duties would not exceed the 15% tariff ceiling agreed under last year's bilateral trade deal. Japan, the European Union, and Taiwan also retain their 15% caps; China faces the highest rate at 20% on top of earlier tariffs. The Korea Herald reports that digital regulations remain a concern for Seoul alongside the overcapacity framing.

also_today.headline: Unification minister nominee Hong Ik-pyo pledges incremental steps over high-level inter-Korean meetings
also_today.body_text: **Hong Ik-pyo**, the former Democratic Party floor leader nominated to lead the Unification Ministry, said he would focus on "lower-level and more realistic dialogue" to ease inter-Korean hostilities rather than high-profile summits. President Lee approved the confirmation hearing request on November 26.

also_today.headline: Dandong announces five-year plan to boost DPRK trade via simplified customs and New Yalu River Bridge
also_today.body_text: The Chinese border city of Dandong's Guomenwan Border Trade Zone announced plans to simplify customs procedures for small-scale border trade and expand use of the New Yalu River Bridge, also inviting border residents within 20 kilometers to register for passes allowing up to 8,000 yuan ($1,200) per day in duty-free imports from North Korea.

also_today.headline: Supreme Court confirms former President Yoon Suk Yeol's acquittal in perjury case
also_today.body_text: The ROK Supreme Court on November 26 upheld the acquittal of former President **Yoon Suk Yeol** on charges he perjured himself during the martial law trial of former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo. An appellate court had upheld the lower court's acquittal in September.

us_korea_deals.state_of_play: Steel and aluminum remain at 50% and automobiles at 15%, both under Section 232. The Section 122 surcharge expired July 24, so there is no baseline reciprocal tariff in effect. Trump's new Section 301 proposal targeting 14 trading partners preserves the 15% ceiling negotiated under last year's US-Korea deal.

business_economy.headline: Korean consumer goods exports reach record $28.65B, with US overtaking China as top market
business_economy.body_text: Korea Customs Service data show consumer goods exports reached *$28.65 billion* from January 1 to November 19, up 21.5% year on year and beating last year's record of $27.02 billion. The United States surpassed China as the largest market for Korean consumer goods for the first time since 2004, with US-bound shipments up 30.3% to $5.69 billion.

business_economy.headline: Starbucks Korea returns to profit after 'Tank Day' backlash
business_economy.body_text: Starbucks Korea reported a return to profit following a consumer boycott that stemmed from the so-called 'Tank Day' controversy. The recovery points to resilience in premium coffee consumption despite broader cost-of-living pressures.

business_economy.headline: Elon Musk sought long-term semiconductor supply deal with Samsung; Lee Jae-yong reportedly asked what more was on offer
business_economy.body_text: Maeil Business reports that Elon Musk approached Samsung Electronics chairman **Lee Jae-yong** with a proposal for a long-term purchase agreement for memory semiconductors, amid AI-driven chip scarcity. Lee reportedly responded by asking what additional terms Musk would offer, with the exchange reflecting intensifying competition for Korean chip supply.

business_economy.headline: Kim Yong-bum named to lead new private capital market reform body
business_economy.body_text: **Kim Yong-bum**, described as a figure from Meritz Financial, was named to head a new private-sector capital market reform organization, with the government granting full authority to the private sector body. The reform body is expected to push for equal voting rights for major and minority shareholders.

northeast_asia.headline: Russian Tu-160 nuclear bombers identified in KADIZ incursion near Ulleung Island; Su-57 presence suspected
northeast_asia.body_text: Russian aircraft that entered South Korea's Korea Air Defense Identification Zone on November 24 were identified as Tu-160 supersonic strategic bombers capable of carrying nuclear weapons, with footage released by Russia's Defense Ministry also capturing an aircraft believed to be a Su-57 stealth fighter, which Seoul's Defense Ministry separately denied was present. Defense experts said the Tu-160 exercise in the East Sea appeared aimed at countering US Pacific forces and establishing early access to Arctic routes.

northeast_asia.headline: China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN launch talks on cross-border digital payments working group
northeast_asia.body_text: Finance officials from China, Japan, South Korea, and ASEAN member states agreed to form a working group on cross-border digital payments under the ASEAN+3 framework. The initiative marks a multilateral effort to reduce friction in intra-regional financial transfers.

rok_government.action: FM Cho Hyun phones Iranian FM Araghchi on Cheonghae unit expansion and Middle East stability
rok_government.detail: FM **Cho Hyun** spoke by phone with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi on November 26, explaining that Seoul's planned expansion of the Cheonghae naval unit's mission is aimed at protecting South Korean nationals and economic interests, not participation in the war. Cho requested Iranian attention to the safety of South Korean nationals and said both sides agreed to continue close communication.

rok_government.action: Deputy FM meets Honduras and Guatemala vice ministers, discusses Korea-Central America FTA ratification
rok_government.detail: First Deputy FM **Park Yoon-joo** met separately with the vice ministers of foreign affairs of Honduras and Guatemala on November 26, urging Honduras to complete ratification of Guatemala's accession to the Korea-Central America Free Trade Agreement and asking Guatemala to leverage its upcoming Central American Integration System chairmanship to advance Korea-Central America cooperation.

rok_government.action: Defense Minister holds roundtable with officers trained at foreign military academies to inform new ROK military academy plans
rok_government.detail: Defense Minister **Kang Shin-chul** met with 16 active-duty officers trained at military academies in the United States, France, Turkey, Germany, and Japan on November 26 to gather input on education systems for developing a new ROK military academy model. The ministry said feedback will be incorporated into the academy's curriculum and structure.

calendar_watch.headline: Justice Ministry accepts additional Prosecutor General nominations through December 9
calendar_watch.detail: The Ministry of Justice announced it is accepting an additional round of recommendations for Prosecutor General candidates through December 9, an unprecedented second call after the initial pool of three finalists was submitted.

rok_assembly.action: Democratic Party states only Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae is targeted in impeachment push; judges' collective resistance noted
rok_assembly.detail: The Democratic Party publicly clarified that the impeachment push targets only Chief Justice **Cho Hee-dae**, responding to collective pushback from judges. The party is reaching out to civil society to build support for the impeachment drive.

overnight_items.body_text: Agreement covers Moscow's highest state secrecy tier; posted quietly on Russian legal portal April 17.

overnight_items.headline: Ukraine's DIU: North Korea paused KN-23 and artillery deliveries to Russia amid October dispute
overnight_items.body_text: Friction reportedly began in October; Russia earlier settled a currency dispute by paying Pyongyang in fuel.

overnight_items.body_text: WPK's Seventh Conference of Cell Secretaries met in Pyongyang; Kim warned 'hostile forces' will escalate schemes.

overnight_items.body_text: DPRK declared Swiss mission head Sylvain Astier persona non grata; Switzerland says it 'regrets' the decision.

overnight_items.body_text: Assembly must complete hearings within 20 days; NIS pick Kang Kum-sil is a former Justice Minister.

overnight_items.headline: Lee touts new deposit system as effective curb on illegal Chinese fishing
overnight_items.body_text: Coast Guard raised maximum deposit to 1.5 billion won from 300 million won; 57 Chinese vessels seized last year.

overnight_items.headline: Police seek arrest warrant for top scorer of certified tax accountant exam in AI-cheating case
overnight_items.body_text: Han admitted using a miniature camera, smartphone, and generative AI; charges include obstruction of official duties.

rok_personnel.detail: Former Democratic Party floor leader **Hong Ik-pyo** was nominated by President Lee as Unification Minister; Lee approved the confirmation hearing request on November 26. Hong told reporters he will pursue incremental inter-Korean engagement over high-level meetings.

rok_personnel.name: Kang Kum-sil
rok_personnel.detail: Former Justice Minister **Kang Kum-sil** was nominated to lead the National Intelligence Service; Lee approved the confirmation hearing request on November 26. The Korea Times reported the NIS change follows a reshuffle announced three days earlier.

rok_personnel.detail: Ruling Democratic Party Rep. **Han Jun-ho** was nominated as interior minister; Lee approved the confirmation hearing request on November 26.

opeds_today.headline: South Korea Favorability Remains Stable Overall as Partisan Views Diverge
opeds_today.authors: Korea Economic Institute of America (KEI) / YouGov
opeds_today.central_argument: Overall US favorability toward South Korea has held at 68% since 2020, but a ten-point partisan gap has opened as Republican favorability dropped sharply from 76% in 2023 to 64% in 2024 and has not recovered.
opeds_today.summary: The 2026 KEI survey finds two-thirds of Americans view South Korea favorably, essentially unchanged since the question was first asked in 2020. Democrats have grown more favorable (69% to 75%) while Republicans have declined from a peak of 76% in 2023 to 64% in 2024, creating a partisan divergence with potential implications for alliance politics in a polarized US environment. Food is the top-cited Korean cultural export, drawing nearly double the interest of beauty products, movies, and pop music combined.

opeds_today.headline: The United States Breaks a Decade of UN Consensus on North Korean Human Rights
opeds_today.summary: The United States abstained on the UN Third Committee vote November 18 that adopted a resolution critical of North Korea's human rights record, the first US abstention since the annual process began in 2005 under George W. Bush. Robert King, a former US Special Envoy for North Korean Human Rights, connects the timing to ongoing signals about a potential Trump-Kim diplomatic opening.

opeds_today.headline: Technology Companies Dominate Advertising at North Korean Football Matches
opeds_today.central_argument: Commercial advertising by domestic technology companies at North Korean sports venues reveals the emergence of consumer-facing digital products as a sanctioned internal market sector in a planned economy.
opeds_today.summary: 38 North's Martyn Williams finds that advertising at North Korean football matches is dominated by domestic technology companies, an unusual phenomenon in a planned economy where there is typically little need for commercial promotion. The findings point to a nascent internal consumer technology market that the regime is apparently permitting to develop. Williams' analysis provides a rare data point on the DPRK's internal economic evolution at a time when external trade data are limited.

top_articles.summary: Kimchaek residents in North Hamgyong Province faced continuous labor mobilization throughout 2026, working state construction projects seven days a week and taking on low-paying side jobs to afford food.

capitol_hill.headline: 22 House Republicans urge USTR to scrutinize South Korea's platform regulation legislation
capitol_hill.body_text: Twenty-two House Republican lawmakers sent a letter to the US Trade Representative urging scrutiny of South Korea's pending platform regulatory legislation, citing concerns about its potential impact on US technology companies operating in the Korean market.

korea_world.headline: South Korea speeds selection of new contractor for Czech nuclear plant after Daewoo-Doosan consortium termination
korea_world.body_text: The industry minister stated that keeping the promise to Czech Republic is the first principle of all Team Korea decisions.

korea_world.headline: South Korea and Saudi Arabia expand joint oil reserve agreement
korea_world.body_text: Seoul and Riyadh agreed to expand their joint oil stockpiling arrangement, with Korea Economic Daily reporting the deal comes amid tensions over Seoul's petrochemical restructuring. The expanded reserves provide South Korea an energy buffer against regional disruptions.

korea_world.headline: OCBC Malaysia and Hana Bank team up to facilitate South Korean investments in Malaysia
korea_world.body_text: OCBC Malaysia and South Korea's Hana Bank signed an agreement to jointly facilitate South Korean corporate investment flows into Malaysia, targeting trade finance and cross-border banking services.
